prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on your needs (budget, whether you want ACA marketplace coverage, HSA-eligible plans, short-term, dental, etc.). I can’t definitively name a single best broker for every self-employed person, but I can help you find the right one and explain how to evaluate them. Quick guidance plus next steps:

What type of help most self‑employed people need
- Enroll in an Individual/Family ACA plan and determine subsidy eligibility
- Pick between HMOs/PPOs, deductibles, networks, and HSA-qualified plans
- Compare alternatives (short-term plans, private plans, professional association plans)
- Understand tax/SEP/1095 reporting and options for retirement- or HSA-linked plans

How to find a good Kansas City, MO broker (recommended approach)
1. Prefer an independent agent/broker who can show multiple carrier options (not captive to a single insurer).
2. Verify licensing with the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance.
3. Look for experience with self‑employed/sole proprietor clients and ACA Qualified Health Plans.
4. Read recent Google/Yelp reviews and ask for client references.
5. Confirm how they’re paid (most get carrier commissions; ask if they charge additional fees).
6. Use free navigators or marketplace-certified brokers if you expect to claim subsidies — those are familiar with healthcare.gov rules.

Where to look right now
- Search “ACA-certified agent Kansas City MO” or “health insurance broker Kansas City MO” and check ratings.
- National/online options that serve individuals: HealthSherpa (marketplace enrollments), eHealth (broad carrier access). These are useful if you want mostly online comparison tools.
- Local resources: NAHU/NAIFA directories, Kansas City Chamber / community health centers for certified application counselors.

Questions to ask any broker before you hire them
- Do you work with self‑employed clients? How many?
- Which carriers and plan types do you represent? Are you independent?
- Can you enroll me in marketplace plans so I can get premium tax credits if eligible?
- How do you get paid? Any broker fees I should know about?
- Can you help with year‑end reporting (1095‑A) or QSEHRA/SEP interactions?
- Do you provide ongoing help for claims and renewals? Is after‑sales support included?

Red flags
- Pushes a single carrier without showing alternatives
- Vague about fees/commissions
- Not willing to show carrier networks or plan detail before you apply
- No verifiable reviews or local references

If you want, I can:
- Look up a short vetted list of Kansas City–area brokers (I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood)
- Prepare a tailored list of questions to ask based on your age, family size, budget, and whether you want marketplace subsidies or an HSA plan

Which would you prefer — that I find local broker names for your ZIP code, or help you choose between online platforms vs local independent brokers?
